newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujimori arrives Japan for APEC membership talks.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori arrives Japan for APEC membership talks.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori, distracted by a killer earthquake back home, arrived in Tokyo on Wednesday and almost immediately went into talks about the Latin American nation joining APEC.
Within hours of his arrival, Fujimori and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto were in discussions about how Peru could join the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
"The main aim (of the meeting) is to lay the groundwork for Peru's participation in APEC," the chief cabinet secretary and government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told reporters.
Fujimori, who is of Japanese ancestry, is making his sixth visit to Japan since becoming president in July 1990.

A moratorium on APEC membership expires this month and the issue of extending it is to be discussed at an APEC ministerial meeting in Manila beginning on November 22 followed by a leader's summit on November 25.
Eleven countries, including Vietnam, Peru and Russia, have applied to become members of the present 18-member APEC. Mexico and Chile are the only Latin American members of the grouping.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.

Earlier on Wednesday in Tokyo, Rizalino Navarro, a special adviser to Philippine President Fidel Ramos on APEC affairs, told Reuters Financial Television his country favoured completely ending the moratorium on new membership.
"Rather than extend the moratorium, our more positive approach is to say we will open up the membership, but adopt some procedures, some criteria of admission," Navarro said.
Fujimori, who learned of the killer earthquake in his country while flying to Tokyo from Lima, was awaiting latest reports on the damage before deciding whether to cut short an 11-day Asian tour.

Asked if he intended returning immediately to Peru because of the quake which caused widespread damage, Fujimori told reporters: "I would have to evaluate (the circumstances) and make appropriate decisions."
"I have given instructions to government authorities to take necessary and urgent measures for those who were caught in that disaster," he added.
After Japan, Fujimori is scheduled to visit the Philippines, Thailand and Malyasia.
The 7.3 Richter scale quake struck at noon local time on Tuesday (1700 GMT, Tuesday) with the epicentre about 100 km (65 miles) southeast of the town of Ica in southern Peru.
It killed at least seven people, injured more than 500 and left tens of thousands of people homeless.
